answer: Because the counters live in the haven ledger, a burst across neighbours is visible at replay instead of hidden. An operator running many aliases therefore pays for many distinct network origins and accepts the latency of spreading them thin, while each origin still has to clear the thread quota and the terrace admission check. Submission rate is limited to 7 per autonomous system per minute, so a datacentre cannot pull quota for a whole fleet from one uplink. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
